title: Auxiliary Power Unit Mount Damping Change for Revised Ground Noise Limits
abstract: Change of the auxiliary power unit mount elastomers and the addition of a tuned absorber at the upper link, to bring ground noise at the stand inside limits that several European airports will apply from 2028.

sections.reason: Four European airports have published ground noise limits taking effect in 2028 that this aircraft does not meet with the auxiliary power unit running at electrical load. The dominant contribution is not the exhaust but structure-borne excitation of the fin root and the aft fuselage skin at the load compressor blade passing frequency, which the current mount elastomers pass through almost unattenuated. Operators serving those airports would otherwise have to take ground power and pre-conditioned air at every turn, which is not available at all stands and would cost turnround time where it is.
sections.description: The mount elastomers are replaced by a two-stage arrangement tuned below the blade passing frequency, and a tuned mass absorber is added at the upper mount link. The sub-assembly clamp D4910116459455 is retained, the superseded upper clamp D4910116261434 is replaced by an item with the absorber boss integrated, and the right-hand mount link sub-assembly D4910116633903 is replaced by a stiffer item so that the absorber tuning is not dominated by link compliance. Barrel nuts LN251117-2E and plain washers LN427759-6B are renewed at every mount position. The installation seal at FIN 2PA8, the clamp at FIN 2PB7, the tube assembly at FIN 5401PA1 and the shroud at FIN 726PB9 are all disturbed for access and are refitted, with only the seal renewed. Work is through the auxiliary power unit compartment and the fin root access in zones 313, 322, 325 and 342. Detail is on drawing D49101121028.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 27 kg per aircraft, well aft, giving a centre-of-gravity shift of 0.07 per cent mean aerodynamic chord aft. No electrical load change. The revised mount is not interchangeable with the original because the link stiffness and the boss are different, and all mount positions must be at the same standard. Predicted benefit is a 6 decibel reduction at the stand measurement point at full electrical load. Vibration survey content and the auxiliary power unit removal and installation tasks both require update, and the compartment access route changes because the absorber occupies part of the previous hand clearance.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only. Provisional estimate is four days with the auxiliary power unit removed, which is normally combined with a scheduled unit change so that the downtime is shared. Kits include the elastomers, the absorber and all mount hardware.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must confirm that the absorber boss does not conflict with the bonding strap installation added to the fin box on the same access route, and whether the vibration survey has to be repeated on aircraft carrying the auxiliary power unit variant with the higher load compressor rating.
